courses.title: ChatGPT Basics for Beginners
courses.desc: Learn what ChatGPT is and isn't, set up your free account in five minutes, write your first 10 useful prompts, and avoid the beginner mistakes that waste time. Designed for Kenyan students, professionals and business owners who want to use AI from their phone — no tech background needed.
courses.tagline: Your first real ChatGPT win in under 2 hours.
courses.preview: ChatGPT is a free AI tool that can draft emails, explain difficult concepts, brainstorm business ideas, and help you write professional documents — all from your phone. In this course you will learn exactly how ChatGPT works, set up your free account in under five minutes, and write your first ten useful prompts for everyday tasks. You will discover the four-part prompt formula — role, context, task, and format — that turns ChatGPT from a novelty into a tool you use daily. The course also covers voice input on your phone for faster prompting, how to save and organise your best prompts, and the three mental rules that prevent you from trusting wrong AI output. By the end you will have a working ChatGPT account, ten ready-to-use prompts, and the confidence to use AI for schoolwork, business ideas, or daily communication.

courses.title: AI Prompt Writing 101

courses.tagline: Stop getting vague answers — write prompts that work first time.
courses.preview: Most people type vague one-line questions into ChatGPT and get vague one-line answers. This course teaches you the structured prompting methods that produce useful, specific output every time. You will learn how to give AI a clear role, provide the right context, specify your desired format, and iterate when the first answer misses the mark. The course includes a prompt repair framework for fixing bad outputs, techniques for getting consistent results across different AI tools, and a library of plug-and-play prompt templates for emails, reports, research, and creative tasks. Whether you use ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini, these skills transfer directly.

I am pasting a [document type — contract, report, article]. Read the entire document and give me: 1. A 5-bullet summary, 2. The 3 most important points, 3. Anything unusual or risky, 4. Recommended next steps.

I am about to sign this contract. Read it carefully and tell me: What am I agreeing to deliver? What are the payment terms? Are there any clauses that put me at risk? What should I try to negotiate? Any missing protections I should ask for?

Here is a transcript of a meeting. Produce one page of minutes with: Key decisions made, Action items (with owner and deadline), Open questions needing follow-up, Any commitments or promises made. Keep names and numbers exact.
I need to reply to these messages. For each, write a reply in my tone — friendly but professional, under 80 words: [paste the messages]
Write my weekly report for [role/business]. Structure: What was completed this week, Challenges or blockers, Plans for next week. Here are my rough points: [paste points]
I need to research [topic] for [purpose]. Break it into 5 focused questions. For each question, tell me what kind of source to look for and what keywords to search. Keep it practical and specific.

Here are notes from 3 articles on [topic]. Extract: Key facts from each article, Where the articles agree, Where they conflict, One practical takeaway per article. Flag anything that needs verification.
Organise this into a table with columns: [list columns]. Fix obvious typos in names, flag missing amounts, and keep the original order: [paste data]
Here are 10 emails I received today (summaries). Sort them into: Reply today (urgent), Reply this week, Delegate, Archive. One line of reason for each decision.

Based on these 3 examples of my writing, write a style guide I can use as Claude instructions. Cover: tone, sentence length, word choices, greeting style, and sign-off style: [paste 3 writing examples]
Here is a proposal I sent that did not win the client. Analyse it: what is weak, what is missing, and what would make it more compelling. Then rewrite the improved version: [paste proposal]
Here are my tasks this month: [list tasks]. Which ones repeat weekly or monthly? For each, suggest a Claude Project setup with the files I would upload and the instructions I would set.

Here is what I accomplished this week: [list]. Here is what I struggled with: [list]. Analyse my week: what should I keep doing, what should I stop, and what one change would save me the most time next week?
Here is a prompt I use and an output I did not like. Suggest specific edits to the prompt so the next output fits me better: [prompt] [bad output]

68.t: I am writing a proposal for [client type] who needs [service]. Here is the job posting: [paste]. Analyse the posting, then write a proposal with: I understand your problem, My approach, What I will deliver, Why me, Next steps. Match the tone of my winning proposals. Under 400 words.

I have a generic proposal draft for a [client type] job. Personalise it with these details about the client: Their business: [describe], A recent project: [link or description], A specific pain point: [detail]. Add 2-3 sentences that show I researched them specifically.

Read this entire contract clause by clause. For each clause: plain-language explanation, what it obligates me to do, what rights it gives me, what risks it creates, whether it is standard for [type of contract]. End with a negotiation priority list.

I am preparing a research brief for [client type] about [topic]. Here is my raw research: [paste]. Create a client-ready brief with: Executive Summary, Market Context, Key Findings, Implications, Recommended Actions. Professional, client-facing tone.

I am writing a grant proposal for [organisation] to [funder]. Project: [cause] in [location]. Create an outline: Problem Statement, Proposed Solution, Target Beneficiaries, Activities and Timeline, Expected Outcomes, Budget Framework, Sustainability Plan. Donor-friendly language.

You are the content strategist for [client]. Brand: [description]. Audience: [description]. Platforms: [list]. Plan this week's content: posts for each platform with format, topic, caption, hashtags, and how it drives [goal]. Match the brand voice.
Write my weekly update to [client name] for the [project]. Completed: [list]. Challenges: [list]. Next week: [list]. Professional, transparent, confident. Under 150 words.

A client asked for [extra request]. Original scope was [scope]. Write a message that acknowledges the request, explains it is out of scope, offers a change order with pricing (KES [amount]), and keeps the relationship warm. Under 100 words.

I am delivering [project type] to [client]. Create a delivery package: cover email, table of contents, 1-page 'How to Use This' guide, and feedback request with 3 questions. Professional tone, exceptional value.

Write 3 payment reminders for Invoice [#] sent [date], amount KES [amount] for [service], client [name]. Version 1 (7 days late): friendly. Version 2 (14 days): firmer. Version 3 (30 days): professional with consequences. All brief and not aggressive.

I am pricing a [service] project. Scope: [describe]. Client budget: [budget or unknown]. Analyse: market rate in Kenya, pricing strategy, 3 pricing options with deliverables, what to charge extra for, scope creep red flags. Give a recommended price with justification.

Here is a project I completed: [describe]. Write a case study: Client challenge, My approach, The solution, Results with metrics, Client quote. Professional tone, 300 words max. Show expertise without bragging.

Here are 6 articles about [industry trend]. Analyse: What the trend is, Why it matters for Kenyan businesses, Evidence with data points, Who benefits and who is at risk, 3 actionable recommendations. Write as a professional industry analysis.

I want to position myself as an expert in [field] on LinkedIn. Here are 3 insights from my work: [list]. For each, write a hook, the insight in 2-3 paragraphs, a takeaway or question, and hashtags. Professional but human, under 200 words per post.

A client wants [service]. Define the scope: what is included in base price, what is extra, what I need from client, realistic timeline with milestones, revision rounds, and what happens if requirements change. Write as a professional scope document.
